events.title: Henry of Flanders defeats the Nicaeans at the Battle of Adramyttion
events.description: Latin crusader forces under Henry of Flanders defeated an army of the Empire of Nicaea, led by Constantine Laskaris, at Adramyttion. Nicaea was one of the Greek states founded after the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204.

events.title: Ugolino di Conti is elected Pope Gregory IX
events.description: Following the death of Pope Honorius III, Ugolino di Conti was elected pope and took the name Gregory IX. He reigned until 1241 and is known for issuing the Decretales and instituting the Papal Inquisition.
events.html: Following the death of Pope Honorius III, Ugolino di Conti was elected pope and took the name Gregory IX. He reigned until 1241 and is known for issuing the Decretales and instituting the Papal Inquisition.

events.title: The Byzantine Empire and Venice renew their treaty
events.description: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Venice renegotiated their treaty of 1268 and extended it for two years. Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos kept the Venetian fleet out of Charles of Anjou's crusade plans, while Venice gained wider trading privileges.

events.title: Mongol fleet destroys the last Song forces at Yamen
events.description: In a sea battle off the Pearl River delta, Yuan forces crushed the Song navy. The minister Lu Xiufu jumped into the sea with the child emperor, completing Kublai Khan's conquest of China.
events.html: In a sea battle off the Pearl River delta, Yuan forces crushed the Song navy. The minister Lu Xiufu jumped into the sea with the child emperor, completing Kublai Khan's conquest of China.

events.title: Edict of Amboise ends the first French War of Religion
events.description: Catherine de' Medici's peace allowed Huguenot nobles to worship freely and others in limited places. Neither side was satisfied, and war resumed in 1567.
events.html: Catherine de' Medici's peace allowed Huguenot nobles to worship freely and others in limited places. Neither side was satisfied, and war resumed in 1567.

events.title: René-Robert de La Salle killed by his own men
events.description: The explorer who had claimed the Mississippi basin for France was shot by mutineers in east Texas after his colony went astray. His Fort Saint Louis was soon destroyed.
events.html: The explorer who had claimed the Mississippi basin for France was shot by mutineers in east Texas after his colony went astray. His Fort Saint Louis was soon destroyed.

events.title: Gounod's 'Faust' premieres in Paris
events.description: Charles Gounod's opera, based on Goethe, opened at the Théâtre Lyrique. Revised with recitatives and a ballet, it became one of the most performed operas of the 19th century.
events.html: Charles Gounod's opera, based on Goethe, opened at the Théâtre Lyrique. Revised with recitatives and a ballet, it became one of the most performed operas of the 19th century.

events.title: US adopts standard time zones and daylight saving time
events.description: The Standard Time Act gave legal force to time zones first used by the railways and introduced daylight saving time to save fuel. Daylight saving proved unpopular and was repealed in 1919.

events.title: Hitler issues the 'Nero Decree'
events.description: Hitler ordered the destruction of German industry, transport and supplies before they fell to the Allies. Armaments Minister Albert Speer worked to ensure it was largely not carried out.
